record.context_brief: Cokernels of Carlitz and Kasteleyn matrices
record.original_question: Let K be the Kasteleyn matrix of an a, b, c semiregular hexagon, and let the associated Carlitz matrix be the b-by-b matrix obtained from K by row and column reductions, with entries given by binomial coefficients. Determine the cokernel of these Carlitz matrices, equivalently the cokernel of the Kasteleyn matrices of a, b, c hexagons, and if possible interpret that cokernel in terms of lozenge tilings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an $a,b,c$ semiregular hexagon: a hexagon with side lengths $a,b,c,a,b,c$ (in cyclic order) drawn on the triangular lattice, whose region is tiled by unit lozenges (rhombi made of two adjacent unit triangles) in three orientations. The lozenge tilings of this hexagon are in bijection with the perfect matchings of its honeycomb dual graph $G_{a,b,c}$.

Let $K = K(a,b,c)$ be the Kasteleyn(–Percus) matrix associated with $G_{a,b,c}$, viewed as an integer matrix whose permanent (up to sign) counts perfect matchings. Through systematic row and column reductions over $\mathbb{Z}$, $K$ can be reduced to a $b \times b$ integer matrix $C = C(a,b,c)$, the Carlitz matrix, whose $(i,j)$ entry is the binomial coefficient
$$
C_{ij} \;=\; \binom{a+c}{a-i+j}, \qquad 1 \le i,j \le b.
$$
Since the row/column reductions are unimodular, the integer cokernels coincide:
$$
\operatorname{coker}(K) \;\cong\; \operatorname{coker}(C) \;=\; \mathbb{Z}^{b}/C\,\mathbb{Z}^{b}.
$$

Problem. Determine the cokernel $\operatorname{coker}(C(a,b,c))$ as a finite abelian group (equivalently, determine the Smith normal form of $C(a,b,c)$) for all positive integers $a,b,c$, and provide a combinatorial interpretation of this cokernel in terms of the lozenge tilings of the $a,b,c$ semiregular hexagon.
artifact.category_tag: Smith normal form of Kasteleyn matrices
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work, notably "Kasteleyn cokernels" (arXiv:math/0108150, Electron. J. Combin. 2002) and later REU notes by Conlon (2022), studies the Smith normal form of these Carlitz matrices. Partial results and conjectures have been obtained (e.g., a characterization of when the cokernel is cyclic, with C(4,2,2), C(2,4,2), C(2,2,4) conjectured to be the only such examples with min(a,b,c) > 1, and the rank of the cokernel bounded by min(a,b,c) via Gessel–Viennot), but no complete general formula or combinatorial interpretation in terms of lozenge tilings appears to be known.

status_evidence.title: Kasteleyn cokernels
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Smith normal form / cokernels of Kasteleyn and Carlitz matrices, with partial results and conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: The problem has been partially addressed with explicit Smith normal form computations and conjectures.

status_evidence.title: On plane partitions and Kasteleyn cokernels
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures C(4,2,2), C(2,4,2), C(2,2,4) are the only Carlitz matrices with cyclic cokernel for min(a,b,c)>1.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2022) REU work continues to investigate the cokernel, indicating the general problem remains open.
